title: Regular local surfaces define rational singularities
statement: Let $R$ be a commutative Nagata regular local ring of Krull dimension $2$ [def-weil-pbc-nagata-ring], [def-weil-regular-scheme], [def-weil-pbc-krull-dimension-ring]. Then $R$ defines a rational singularity [def-per-rational-surface-singularity].

proof.text: By [lem-weil-pbc-regular-local-localization], $R$ is a regular ring. Thus [lem-weil-pbc-regular-ring-normal] makes it normal, and [lem-sc-regular-local-domain] makes it a domain. Noetherianity is part of regular locality [def-weil-regular-scheme]. In particular $R$ satisfies the ambient conditions of [def-per-rational-surface-singularity]. Put $S=\operatorname{Spec}R$ and denote its closed point by $s$. Its affine coordinate ring is regular, so $S$ is regular [def-weil-regular-scheme]; it is integral [def-pc-integral-scheme] since that ring is a domain, and is Noetherian. Fix an arbitrary normal modification $f:Z\to S$ as in [def-per-rational-surface-singularity]. It remains to prove $H^1(Z,\mathcal O_Z)=0$.

source.place: Tag 0B4Q, ambient hypotheses and the sentence fixing a normal modification; regular-local localization is algebra.tex Tag 0AFS.

proof.text: The morphism $f$ is an isomorphism over $S\setminus\{s\}$. Indeed, every nonmaximal prime of the two-dimensional local domain $R$ has height at most one: a chain of length two ending at a nonmaximal prime could be prolonged by the maximal ideal, contradicting $\dim R=2$. At a height-one prime the local ring is regular by [lem-weil-pbc-regular-local-localization] and is a DVR by [lem-sc-regular-dim1-dvr]. Apply clauses (1) and (2) of [lem-per-normal-modification-codimension-one]: its Noetherian-target hypothesis holds for $S$, and its reduced-source hypothesis holds because $Z$ is integral. Hence its isomorphism open contains every point other than $s$.

source.place: Tag 0B4Q, preparation for domination; resolve-situation-vanishing and the following paragraph, using varieties.tex Tag 0BFP.

proof.text: Apply [lem-per-regular-point-blowup-domination] to $X=S$, $Y=Z$, and $T=\{s\}$. The set $T$ is finite and closed, and $\mathcal O_{S,s}=R$ is regular local of dimension two. The isomorphism away from $T$ was proved in Step 2. We obtain $X_n\xrightarrow{b_n}\cdots\xrightarrow{b_1}X_0=S$ and $h:X_n\to Z$ over $S$, with each center a reduced closed point lying above $s$.

source.place: Tag 0B4Q, first paragraph, domination by Tag 0AHI.

proof.text: Induct on $i$ to check that $X_i$ is integral, regular and Noetherian, its map to $S$ is proper and birational, and every closed point above $s$ has a local ring of dimension two. The base $X_0=S$ has these properties by Step 1, and its only point above $s$ is $s$. For the induction step the next center $p_i$ is one of these closed points. Apply [lem-per-regular-point-blowup-acyclic]. It gives the asserted integrality, regularity and Noetherianity of $X_{i+1}$, properness of $b_{i+1}$, and the isomorphism off $p_i$, so the composite to $S$ remains proper by [lem-weil-pbc-proper-composition] and birational by its unchanged generic point and function field. If a closed point $q$ above $s$ maps to $p_i$, its local dimension is two by the same cited statement. Otherwise its local ring is unchanged by the isomorphism away from $p_i$; its image is closed since $b_{i+1}$ is proper, and the induction hypothesis gives dimension two there. This completes the induction. Every $X_i$ is also normal by clause (1) of [rem-pc-regular-normal]. The same blowup result gives $R^1(b_i)_*\mathcal O_{X_i}=0$ for every $1\leq i\leq n$.

source.place: Tag 0B4Q, regularity sentence and last sentence, using Tags 0AGR and 0AGS.

proof.text: The affine-vanishing statement [lem-pc-affine-vanishing] applied to the structure sheaf on $X_0=S$ gives $H^1(X_0,\mathcal O_{X_0})=0$. Inductively suppose $H^1(X_{i-1},\mathcal O_{X_{i-1}})=0$. Apply [lem-per-modification-h1-exact-sequence] with base $R$, target modification $X_{i-1}\to S$, source modification $X_i\to S$, and comparison $b_i$. Step 4 gives normality of the target and both modification hypotheses. Its right-hand term $H^0(X_{i-1},R^1(b_i)_*\mathcal O_{X_i})$ is zero by Step 4. Exactness then forces the middle term $H^1(X_i,\mathcal O_{X_i})$ to vanish. Thus $H^1(X_n,\mathcal O_{X_n})=0$, also when $n=0$.

source.place: Tag 0B4Q, reduction to the vanishing of the first direct images via Tag 0AXF; affine base case made explicit.

proof.text: Apply [lem-per-modification-h1-exact-sequence] to $Z\to S$, $X_n\to S$, and $h:X_n\to Z$. The target $Z$ is normal by its choice in Step 1, and Step 4 gives the source modification. The left arrow is an injection $H^1(Z,\mathcal O_Z)\hookrightarrow H^1(X_n,\mathcal O_{X_n})$. Step 5 makes its target zero, so its source is zero. Since $Z$ was an arbitrary normal modification, [def-per-rational-surface-singularity] gives that $R$ defines a rational singularity.

source.place: Tag 0B4Q, injection by Tag 0AXF and conclusion by Tag 0B4N.
